children.name: Ischnochiton maorianus
children.description: Ischnochiton maorianus, sometimes called the variable chiton, is a fast moving species of chiton in the family Ischnochitonidae, endemic to the main islands of New Zealand where it is abundant.

children.name: Ischnochiton torri
children.description: Ischnochiton torri, commonly known as Torr's ischnochiton, is a species of chiton in the genus Ischnochiton that lives under rocks in the intertidal and shallow subtidal waters of southern Australia.

children.name: Ischnochiton lineolatus
children.description: Ischnochiton lineolatus, commonly known as the lined ischnochiton is a species of chiton in the genus Ischnochiton that lives under rocks in the intertidal waters of southern and south-western Australia, from Bass Strait to the central west coast.

children.name: Lepidozona mertensii
children.description: Lepidozona mertensii, Merten's chiton, is a species of chiton found under intertidal rocks from northern Alaska to northern Mexico.

children.name: Lepidozona cooperi
children.description: Lepidozona cooperi, commonly known as Cooper's chiton, is a common species of chiton found among intertidal rocks and boulders from Vancouver Island to Baja California.

children.name: Stenoplax heathiana
children.description: Stenoplax heathiana, commonly known as Heath's chiton, is a species of chiton found under rocks in the sandy middle and low intertidal, from Mendocino County, CA to Puerto Santo Tomás, Baja California.

children.name: Stenoplax conspicua
children.description: Stenoplax conspicua, the conspicuous chiton, is a species of polyplacophoran mollusc belonging to the family Ischnochitonidae.

children.name: Stenochiton longicymba
children.description: Stenochiton longicymba, the clasping stenochiton is a species of polyplacophoran mollusc with an elongated shell, in the family Ishnochitonidae.

children.name: Nuttallochiton mirandus
children.description: Nuttallochiton mirandus is a medium to large-sized species of polyplacophoran mollusc in the family Mopaliidae.
